newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GINOLA MAGIC CAPS 4-0 WIN FOR NEWCASTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GINOLA MAGIC CAPS 4-0 WIN FOR NEWCASTLE.

text.p: An unstoppable volley from David Ginola and a pair of goals from Colombian Faustino Asprilla helped Newcastle to a 4-0 victory over Ferencvaros of Hungary in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday.
Les Ferdinand scored Newcastle's fourth in injury time to give Kevin Keegan's side a 6-3 aggregate win which takes them into the third round.

Ginola, who scored with an outstanding right-foot drive in Newcastle's 5-0 defeat of Manchester United last weekend, excelled even that strike after Asprilla had sewn up the tie with a goal in each half.

The Frenchman, lurking on the edge of the penalty area, trapped a loose ball on his right thigh, teed it up with the inside of his right foot, and blasted a left-foot volley into the top left-hand corner of Jozef Szeller's net.

The goal confirmed Ginola's recent return to form after a barren spell which saw him dropped or substituted from the Newcastle side for five consecutive league matches prior to the memorable clash with United.
"It was one of my best," he acknowledged afterwards.
Asprilla had dominated Newcastle's forward play up until that point.
After a frustrating first 40 minutes in which Peter Beardsley missed a penalty, the Colombian put the home side ahead with a opportunist goal from close range.

Taking full advantage of his place in the side through the absence of injured team mate Alan Shearer, he added his second just before the hour, calmly side-footing a shot past Szeller after finding himself free in the Ferencvaros box.

The Hungarians, who actually led the tie 2-0 early in the first leg, wilted in the second half and Newcastle surged forward to take their goal-tally from their last two games at St James' Park to nine.
